title: Whole Milk 1 gal

drivers.name: Price increase (5.1%)
drivers.evidence: Previous price increase to $4.56 led to 119 units (52% below baseline). Noise-adjusted post-promo effect shows 5% drop after discount, implying symmetric sensitivity. This is a new high price, but behavior consistent with demand elasticity.

drivers.name: Heatwave (38°C)
drivers.evidence: No past heatwave data, but dairy consumption declines in extreme heat. Plausible, but unconfirmed. Evidence is weak, so effect shrunk. Combined with price, it reinforces downward pressure.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 207.6. A 5.1% price increase to $4.56 (from $4.34) is observed, with no promotion. Recent weeks show a drop to 119 units after a prior price hike (2026-10-05), suggesting a price sensitivity effect. The noise-adjusted price sensitivity from past promotions is x0.95 for the week after a discount, but here the price is rising. No past price increase at this level is observed. The heatwave forecast (38°C) may reduce demand due to reduced dairy consumption in extreme heat. No past heatwave data is available, so evidence is thin. The classical model suggests no uplift, but judgment overrides it. We apply a downward adjustment for price and heat, shrunk due to low evidence. Median adjusted down, spreads widened slightly for uncertainty.

  median 207.6 | 5%-95%: 133.8 - 290.0 | 10%-90%: 156.5 - 280.8

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-22% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
